Build an 8-slide, 16:9 PowerPoint presentation titled "State of the Web 2020–2025: HTTP Archive Trends in Page Weight, Protocols, and Security" for web performance engineers and front-end architects evaluating infrastructure trends.

The deck should open with a title slide establishing the HTTP Archive data source and time range, then progress through the growth in crawl sample size, rising page weight trends, request and connection efficiency metrics, near-universal HTTPS adoption, HTTP/2 vs. HTTP/3 protocol shifts, and font-display CSS adoption. Close with a key takeaways slide that synthesizes the five major findings and calls the audience to benchmark their own sites against these baselines. The tone throughout should be data-forward, analytical, and technical.

For the "Crawl Sample Size Tripled" slide, include a dual-line time-series chart showing desktop and mobile URL counts over time. For the "HTTPS Requests Reach 99%" slide, feature a prominent large stat callout (99%+) alongside a small time-series line showing the climb from ~80% to 99%. The "Requests and Connections" slide should use a split layout with a stat card for request counts and a declining line chart for TCP connections.

Do not fabricate any data points, percentages, or figures not found in source_brief.md. All metrics cited on slides must directly reference values provided in the brief.


## Data Sources

1. **Read `/app/benchmark/source_brief.md`**  for all the subject-matter text, data tables, statistics, and figure references you may use in the presentation.
2. **Read `/app/benchmark/task_input.json`**  for **structural requirements**: deck metadata (slide count, aspect ratio, audience, tone) and a per-slide outline (id, title, objective) that your presentation must follow.

## Output Requirements

Save the final PPT to `/app/output/final_deck.pptx`.

Only the correctly saved final file is needed — no additional explanation is required.

---

## Automated Execution Rules

There is no human operator online for this session. Follow these rules:

1. **Skip all confirmation/approval/user-input steps** — do not pause, ask questions, or wait for a reply. When encountering BLOCKING or "wait for user confirmation" instructions, make a professional judgment and proceed.
2. **Design decisions** — if `task_input.json` specifies fields such as `deck.tone` or `deck.audience`, use them to guide template, color palette, and style choices; otherwise, use your professional judgment.
3. **Do not deploy or share** — no deployment, PDF export, share links, or other post-delivery steps are needed.
4. **Priority** — these rules take precedence over any interactive-wait instructions in SKILL.md. The workflow, quality standards, and technical specifications in SKILL.md remain in effect; only interactive waits are skipped.

# State of the Web 2020–2025: HTTP Archive Trends

## Source

HTTP Archive — State of the Web Report  
https://httparchive.org/reports/state-of-the-web?start=2020_01_01&end=latest&view=list

## Overview

The HTTP Archive continuously crawls millions of URLs and records how the web is built. The "State of the Web" report tracks macro-level metrics including page weight, request counts, protocol adoption (HTTPS, HTTP/2, HTTP/3), TCP connection counts, and CSS best-practice adoption such as `font-display`. The data below covers January 2020 through early 2026, with desktop and mobile measured separately.

## Sample Size

The crawl sample has grown substantially. In January 2020 the desktop crawl covered roughly 5 million URLs and mobile roughly 3.5 million. By mid-2022 both lines jumped sharply — desktop reaching ~15 million and mobile ~10 million — before stabilizing around 16 million (desktop) and 12.5 million (mobile) by mid-2023 onward.

![Timeseries of Sample Size — Desktop vs Mobile](./assets/figure_1.jpg)

## Page Weight & Requests

Median total transfer size has risen gradually over five years. Desktop pages now weigh approximately 2,000 KB (median), up from ~1,600 KB in early 2020. Mobile pages track slightly lower but follow the same upward trend. The 75th-percentile desktop page exceeds 4,000 KB, indicating a long tail of heavy pages.

![Timeseries of Total Kilobytes — Desktop vs Mobile with IQR bands](./assets/figure_2.jpg)

The median number of resources requested per page is 76 on desktop and 71 on mobile, each up roughly 3% over the observation period.

| Metric | Desktop | Mobile | Desktop Δ | Mobile Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Total Kilobytes (median) | ~2,000 KB | ~1,900 KB | ▲ ~25% | ▲ ~25% |
| Total Requests (median) | 76 | 71 | ▲ 2.7% | ▲ 2.9% |
| TCP Connections / Page (median) | 12.0 | 11.0 | ▼ 14.3% | ▼ 26.7% |

## TCP Connections Per Page

Despite growing request counts, the median number of TCP connections per page has fallen — from about 15 (desktop) and 15 (mobile) in early 2020 to 12 and 11 respectively. This decline reflects the multiplexing benefits of HTTP/2 and HTTP/3, which allow many requests over fewer connections.

![Timeseries of TCP Connections Per Page](./assets/figure_3.jpg)

## Protocol & Security Adoption

### HTTPS

HTTPS adoption is now effectively universal. 99.2% of desktop requests and 99.1% of mobile requests use HTTPS, representing an increase of roughly 19–20 percentage points since early 2020 when adoption was around 80%.

### HTTP/2

HTTP/2 accounts for 58.6% of desktop requests and 57.6% of mobile requests. Growth has been modest recently (1–3%), partly because HTTP/3 is absorbing some of the newer adoption.

### HTTP/3 Support

HTTP/3 support has seen explosive growth. Desktop support stands at 38.7% and mobile at 40.0%. The percentage increases from the 2020 baseline are enormous (reported as 38,600% desktop and 5,614% mobile) because the starting point was near zero. Note: HTTP Archive measures HTTP/3 *support* rather than actual usage because fresh Chrome instances default to HTTP/2 on first connection before discovering HTTP/3 capability via Alt-Svc headers.

| Protocol Metric | Desktop | Mobile |
|---|---|---|
| HTTPS Requests | 99.2% | 99.1% |
| HTTP/2 Requests | 58.6% | 57.6% |
| HTTP/3 Support | 38.7% | 40.0% |

## Font-Display Adoption

The `font-display` CSS property helps avoid the Flash of Invisible Text (FOIT) during web font loading. As measured by Lighthouse, 40.1% of desktop pages and 42.5% of mobile pages now use this property — up 14.9% and 61.0% respectively since 2020. While adoption is growing, more than half of pages still risk FOIT.

## Key Findings

- **Page weight keeps climbing**: Median desktop pages now transfer ~2,000 KB, roughly 25% heavier than in 2020, driven by richer media and JavaScript.
- **HTTPS is the new baseline**: At 99%+ of requests, unencrypted HTTP is essentially extinct on the modern web.
- **HTTP/3 is the fastest-growing protocol metric**: From near-zero to ~40% support in under four years, HTTP/3 is rapidly becoming mainstream.
- **Fewer TCP connections despite more requests**: Multiplexing in HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 has cut median connections per page by 15–27%, improving network efficiency.
- **Font-display still underused**: At ~40–42% adoption, there is significant room for improvement in avoiding invisible text during font loading.

import collections
import collections.abc
from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN
from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
from pptx.enum.chart import XL_LEGEND_POSITION
import os

prs = Presentation()
prs.slide_width = Inches(16)
prs.slide_height = Inches(9)

# Theme colors
DARK_BG = RGBColor(30, 30, 30)
TEXT_COLOR = RGBColor(230, 230, 230)
ACCENT_COLOR = RGBColor(70, 130, 180) # Steel blue

def apply_dark_bg(slide):
    background = slide.background
    fill = background.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = DARK_BG

def add_title(slide, text):
    title_shape = slide.shapes.title
    title_shape.text = text
    title_shape.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.color.rgb = TEXT_COLOR
    title_shape.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(40)
    title_shape.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True
    title_shape.left = Inches(1)
    title_shape.top = Inches(0.5)
    title_shape.width = Inches(14)
    title_shape.height = Inches(1.5)
    return title_shape

# Slide 1: Title
slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[0] # Title layout
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
apply_dark_bg(slide)
title = slide.shapes.title
subtitle = slide.placeholders[1]

title.text = "State of the Web 2020–2025:\nHTTP Archive Trends in Page Weight, Protocols, and Security"
title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.color.rgb = TEXT_COLOR
title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(54)
title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True
if len(title.text_frame.paragraphs) > 1:
    title.text_frame.paragraphs[1].font.color.rgb = TEXT_COLOR
    title.text_frame.paragraphs[1].font.size = Pt(54)
    title.text_frame.paragraphs[1].font.bold = True

subtitle.text = "Based on HTTP Archive Data (Jan 2020 – Mar 2026)\n\nPrepared for Web Performance Engineers and Front-End Architects"
subtitle.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.color.rgb = RGBColor(180, 180, 180)
subtitle.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(28)

# Slide 2: Sample Size
slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[5] # Blank/Title only
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
apply_dark_bg(slide)
add_title(slide, "Crawl Sample Size Tripled: From ~5M to 16M Desktop URLs Since 2020")

# Add text
txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(1), Inches(2), Inches(5), Inches(6))
tf = txBox.text_frame
p = tf.paragraphs[0]
p.text = "Explosive Growth in Crawl Volume:"
p.font.color.rgb = TEXT_COLOR
p.font.size = Pt(24)
p.font.bold = True
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "• Jan 2020: ~5M desktop, ~3.5M mobile"
p.font.color.rgb = TEXT_COLOR
p.font.size = Pt(20)
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "• Mid-2022: Sharp jump to ~15M desktop, ~10M mobile"
p.font.color.rgb = TEXT_COLOR
p.font.size = Pt(20)
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "• Mid-2023 onward: Stabilized at ~16M desktop, 12.5M mobile"
p.font.color.rgb = TEXT_COLOR
p.font.size = Pt(20)

# Add image
img_path = '/app/benchmark/assets/figure_1.jpg'
if os.path.exists(img_path):
    slide.shapes.add_picture(img_path, Inches(6.5), Inches(2.5), width=Inches(8))

# Slide 3: Page Weight
slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[5]
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
apply_dark_bg(slide)
add_title(slide, "Median Page Weight Climbs Steadily to ~2,000 KB on Desktop")

# Add text
txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(1), Inches(2), Inches(5), Inches(6))
tf = txBox.text_frame
p = tf.paragraphs[0]
p.text = "Page Weight Trends (2020-2026):"
p.font.color.rgb = TEXT_COLOR
p.font.size = Pt(24)
p.font.bold = True
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "• Median desktop page grew from ~1,600 KB to ~2,000 KB (▲ ~25%)."
p.font.color.rgb = TEXT_COLOR
p.font.size = Pt(20)
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "• Mobile tracks slightly lower (~1,900 KB) but with similar growth (▲ ~25%)."
p.font.color.rgb = TEXT_COLOR
p.font.size = Pt(20)
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "• 75th percentile on desktop exceeds 4,000 KB."
p.font.color.rgb = TEXT_COLOR
p.font.size = Pt(20)

# Add image
img_path = '/app/benchmark/assets/figure_2.jpg'
if os.path.exists(img_path):
    slide.shapes.add_picture(img_path, Inches(6.5), Inches(2.5), width=Inches(8))

# Slide 4: Requests and Connections
slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[5]
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
apply_dark_bg(slide)
add_title(slide, "76 Requests per Desktop Page While TCP Connections Drop to 12")

# Left: Stat card for Requests
txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(1), Inches(2.5), Inches(6), Inches(4))
txBox.fill.solid()
txBox.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor(50, 50, 50)
tf = txBox.text_frame
p = tf.paragraphs[0]
p.text = "Median Total Requests"
p.font.color.rgb = TEXT_COLOR
p.font.size = Pt(28)
p.font.bold = True
p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "Desktop: 76 (▲ 2.7%)"
p.font.color.rgb = ACCENT_COLOR
p.font.size = Pt(40)
p.font.bold = True
p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "Mobile: 71 (▲ 2.9%)"
p.font.color.rgb = ACCENT_COLOR
p.font.size = Pt(40)
p.font.bold = True
p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER

# Right: Line chart image for TCP Connections
txBox2 = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(8), Inches(1.8), Inches(7), Inches(1))
tf2 = txBox2.text_frame
p2 = tf2.paragraphs[0]
p2.text = "Multiplexing Efficiency (HTTP/2 & HTTP/3)"
p2.font.color.rgb = TEXT_COLOR
p2.font.size = Pt(20)

img_path = '/app/benchmark/assets/figure_3.jpg'
if os.path.exists(img_path):
    slide.shapes.add_picture(img_path, Inches(8), Inches(2.5), width=Inches(7))

# Slide 5: HTTPS
slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[5]
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
apply_dark_bg(slide)
add_title(slide, "HTTPS Requests Reach 99%: Encryption Is Now the Default")

# Stat callout
txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(1.5), Inches(3), Inches(5), Inches(3))
tf = txBox.text_frame
p = tf.paragraphs[0]
p.text = "99.2%"
p.font.color.rgb = ACCENT_COLOR
p.font.size = Pt(120)
p.font.bold = True
p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "Desktop Requests use HTTPS"
p.font.color.rgb = TEXT_COLOR
p.font.size = Pt(24)
p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "(99.1% on Mobile)"
p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(180, 180, 180)
p.font.size = Pt(20)
p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER

# Native chart for time series
chart_data = CategoryChartData()
chart_data.categories = ['2020', '2021', '2022', '2023', '2024', '2025']
chart_data.add_series('HTTPS Adoption', (80, 88, 93, 96, 98, 99.2))

x, y, cx, cy = Inches(7.5), Inches(2.5), Inches(7), Inches(5)
chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(
    XL_CHART_TYPE.LINE, x, y, cx, cy, chart_data
).chart
chart.has_legend = False
chart.value_axis.minimum_scale = 75
chart.value_axis.maximum_scale = 100
# Format chart text
for tick_label in chart.category_axis.tick_labels:
    tick_label.font.color.rgb = TEXT_COLOR
    tick_label.font.size = Pt(14)
for tick_label in chart.value_axis.tick_labels:
    tick_label.font.color.rgb = TEXT_COLOR
    tick_label.font.size = Pt(14)


# Slide 6: HTTP/2 vs HTTP/3
slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[5]
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
apply_dark_bg(slide)
add_title(slide, "HTTP/2 Holds at ~58% While HTTP/3 Support Surges to 40%")

# Stacked/Grouped bar chart
chart_data = CategoryChartData()
chart_data.categories = ['Desktop', 'Mobile']
chart_data.add_series('HTTP/2', (58.6, 57.6))
chart_data.add_series('HTTP/3 Support', (38.7, 40.0))

x, y, cx, cy = Inches(1.5), Inches(2.5), Inches(8), Inches(5)
chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(
    XL_CHART_TYPE.COLUMN_CLUSTERED, x, y, cx, cy, chart_data
).chart
chart.has_legend = True
chart.legend.position = XL_LEGEND_POSITION.TOP
chart.legend.font.color.rgb = TEXT_COLOR
chart.legend.font.size = Pt(16)
for tick_label in chart.category_axis.tick_labels:
    tick_label.font.color.rgb = TEXT_COLOR
    tick_label.font.size = Pt(16)
for tick_label in chart.value_axis.tick_labels:
    tick_label.font.color.rgb = TEXT_COLOR
    tick_label.font.size = Pt(14)

# Text box for context
txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(10), Inches(2.5), Inches(5), Inches(4))
tf = txBox.text_frame
p = tf.paragraphs[0]
p.text = "Explosive Growth:"
p.font.color.rgb = TEXT_COLOR
p.font.size = Pt(24)
p.font.bold = True
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "• HTTP/3 support grew from near zero in 2020 to ~40% today."
p.font.color.rgb = TEXT_COLOR
p.font.size = Pt(20)
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "• HTTP/2 growth is modest (1-3%) as HTTP/3 absorbs new adoption."
p.font.color.rgb = TEXT_COLOR
p.font.size = Pt(20)
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "*Note: Measures support, not usage. Fresh Chrome instances default to HTTP/2 before discovering HTTP/3."
p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(180, 180, 180)
p.font.size = Pt(16)


# Slide 7: Font-Display
slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[5]
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
apply_dark_bg(slide)
add_title(slide, "Font-Display Usage Reaches 42% on Mobile, Up 61% Since 2020")

# Bar chart
chart_data = CategoryChartData()
chart_data.categories = ['Desktop', 'Mobile']
chart_data.add_series('Current Adoption', (40.1, 42.5))
chart_data.add_series('Growth Since 2020', (14.9, 61.0))

x, y, cx, cy = Inches(1.5), Inches(2.5), Inches(8), Inches(5)
chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(
    XL_CHART_TYPE.BAR_CLUSTERED, x, y, cx, cy, chart_data
).chart
chart.has_legend = True
chart.legend.position = XL_LEGEND_POSITION.TOP
chart.legend.font.color.rgb = TEXT_COLOR
chart.legend.font.size = Pt(16)
for tick_label in chart.category_axis.tick_labels:
    tick_label.font.color.rgb = TEXT_COLOR
    tick_label.font.size = Pt(16)
for tick_label in chart.value_axis.tick_labels:
    tick_label.font.color.rgb = TEXT_COLOR
    tick_label.font.size = Pt(14)

txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(10), Inches(2.5), Inches(5), Inches(4))
tf = txBox.text_frame
p = tf.paragraphs[0]
p.text = "FOIT Avoidance:"
p.font.color.rgb = TEXT_COLOR
p.font.size = Pt(24)
p.font.bold = True
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "• The font-display CSS property prevents the Flash of Invisible Text (FOIT)."
p.font.color.rgb = TEXT_COLOR
p.font.size = Pt(20)
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "• Mobile adoption surged 61% to reach 42.5%."
p.font.color.rgb = TEXT_COLOR
p.font.size = Pt(20)
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "• Still, over 50% of pages risk invisible text during web font loading."
p.font.color.rgb = TEXT_COLOR
p.font.size = Pt(20)


# Slide 8: Key Takeaways
slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[5]
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
apply_dark_bg(slide)
add_title(slide, "Key Takeaways: Bigger Pages, Smarter Protocols, Stronger Security")

txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(1.5), Inches(2.5), Inches(13), Inches(5))
tf = txBox.text_frame
tf.word_wrap = True

def add_takeaway(tf, bold_text, normal_text):
    p = tf.add_paragraph()
    p.level = 0
    p.space_before = Pt(14)
    run = p.add_run()
    run.text = bold_text + ": "
    run.font.bold = True
    run.font.color.rgb = ACCENT_COLOR
    run.font.size = Pt(24)
    
    run2 = p.add_run()
    run2.text = normal_text
    run2.font.color.rgb = TEXT_COLOR
    run2.font.size = Pt(24)

# We have 5 takeaways
p = tf.paragraphs[0]
p.text = "Page weight continues to grow"
p.font.bold = True
p.font.color.rgb = ACCENT_COLOR
p.font.size = Pt(24)
run2 = p.add_run()
run2.text = ": Median desktop pages transfer ~2,000 KB (up 25%)."
run2.font.bold = False
run2.font.color.rgb = TEXT_COLOR
run2.font.size = Pt(24)

add_takeaway(tf, "HTTPS is effectively universal", "At 99%+ of requests, plaintext HTTP is extinct.")
add_takeaway(tf, "HTTP/3 support is surging", "Fastest-growing metric, reaching ~40% support from near-zero.")
add_takeaway(tf, "TCP connections are declining", "Multiplexing reduces connections by 15–27% despite more requests.")
add_takeaway(tf, "Font-display has room to grow", "Adoption is ~40-42%, meaning many sites still suffer from FOIT.")

p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.space_before = Pt(30)
p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER
run = p.add_run()
run.text = "Action: Benchmark your own sites against these baselines to prioritize optimization."
run.font.bold = True
run.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(255, 200, 100) # Highlight color
run.font.size = Pt(28)

prs.save('/app/output/final_deck.pptx')
print("Saved to /app/output/final_deck.pptx")
EOF
